name: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
abstract: Atlas API returned 503s under burst traffic because the Postgres connection pool was exhausted by long-lived transactions.
overview: Burst traffic opened transactions that stayed open across an external HTTP call, holding pool slots.
content: Root cause: a transaction wrapped an outbound payment-provider call. Under burst load every pool slot was held waiting on that call. Fix: move the external call outside the transaction and set a statement timeout.

name: Pool size fixed at 20 per instance
abstract: Chose a Postgres connection pool size of 20 per instance rather than autoscaling it.
overview: Pool size is bounded by Postgres max_connections divided by peak instance count.
content: With max_connections 200 and a peak of 8 instances, 20 per instance leaves headroom for migrations and admin sessions. Autoscaling the pool was rejected because it hides exhaustion instead of surfacing it.

name: Always set a statement timeout on pooled connections
abstract: Every pooled Postgres connection sets statement_timeout so a stuck query cannot hold a pool slot forever.
overview: An unbounded query is indistinguishable from a deadlock from the pool's perspective.
content: Set statement_timeout at connection setup, not per query. A slot held by a stuck query is a slot removed from the pool permanently.

name: JWT validation failing due to clock skew
abstract: Token validation intermittently rejected valid JWTs because worker clocks drifted ahead of the issuer.
overview: Workers without NTP drifted up to 40s, so freshly issued tokens looked future-dated.
content: Symptom: sporadic 401s clustered on two hosts. Root cause: nbf claim checked against a skewed clock. Fix: enable NTP and allow 60s leeway on nbf and exp.

name: Refresh tokens rotate on every use
abstract: Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on each exchange, with reuse detection revoking the family.
overview: Rotation limits the blast radius of a stolen refresh token.
content: On each refresh the old token is invalidated and a new one issued. Presenting an already-used refresh token revokes the entire token family, which detects replay.

name: Session store is Redis with 14-day TTL
abstract: Atlas keeps server-side sessions in Redis keyed by session id with a 14-day sliding TTL.
overview: Sessions are server-side so they can be revoked immediately.
content: Redis cluster atlas-sessions. Keys expire after 14 days of inactivity; each authenticated request refreshes the TTL.

name: Migrations run before the new image rolls out
abstract: Schema migrations are applied as a separate job that must succeed before any new pods are created.
overview: Coupling migrations to pod startup causes partial rollouts against a half-migrated schema.
content: The deploy pipeline runs a migration job to completion, then triggers the rollout. Migrations must be backward compatible for one release so the old image keeps working.

name: Rollbacks are only safe within one release
abstract: Because migrations are backward compatible for exactly one release, rollback is only supported one version back.
overview: Two-version rollback would hit schema the old code cannot read.
content: Any destructive migration must be split across two releases: add-and-backfill first, drop in the next. This is what bounds the rollback window.

name: CLI startup regressed to 400ms after adding config discovery
abstract: Beacon CLI cold start went from 40ms to 400ms because config discovery stat-ed every parent directory.
overview: Directory walk ran on every invocation, including trivial commands like --version.
content: Fix: cache the resolved config path and skip discovery entirely for commands that do not read config. Startup returned to 45ms.

name: Distinct exit codes for user error vs internal error
abstract: Beacon returns 2 for user/usage errors and 70 for internal failures so scripts can branch on them.
overview: A single non-zero exit code makes automation unable to distinguish retryable failures.
content: Exit 0 success, 2 usage error, 70 internal error. Anything wrapping beacon retries only on 70.

name: Colour output disabled when not a TTY
abstract: Beacon suppresses ANSI colour when stdout is not a terminal, and honours NO_COLOR.
overview: Colour codes corrupt piped output and log files.
content: Detect with isatty on stdout. NO_COLOR set to any value disables colour regardless of TTY.

name: Stale lock files blocked beacon after a crash
abstract: A crashed beacon left a lock file behind and every later run refused to start.
overview: The lock recorded only a timestamp, so a crash was indistinguishable from a live run.
content: Fix: record the pid in the lock and check liveness with kill -0 before honouring it. A lock whose pid is gone is removed and the run proceeds.

name: Use kernel state not timestamps for run-once gates
abstract: Do-not-run-twice guards must query kernel state such as pgrep or kill -0, never file mtime.
overview: A timestamp gate is a cooldown, not a mutex, and cannot prevent concurrent starts.
content: Timestamps answer 'did this run recently'. Only kernel process state answers 'is this running now'. Conflating them causes stampedes.

name: Exponential backoff with jitter on all retries
abstract: Every beacon retry loop uses exponential backoff with full jitter, capped at 30s.
overview: Synchronised retries from many clients produce thundering herds.
content: sleep = random(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)). Full jitter measurably outperformed equal jitter for our client counts.

name: Require proof of work in code review
abstract: Reviews ask for evidence a change was actually run, not just that it compiles.
overview: A diff that builds is not a diff that works.
content: Every PR description should include the command run and its output. Reviewers reject 'should work' claims without evidence.

name: Conventional commits with a why-focused body
abstract: Commit subjects follow conventional-commit style; bodies explain why, not what.
overview: The diff already shows what changed.
content: type(scope): subject under 72 chars. Body explains the reason for the change and any rejected alternative.

name: Reclaiming disk from simulator runtimes
abstract: The largest disk consumer on this machine was old iOS simulator runtimes under CoreSimulator.
overview: Xcode retains every simulator runtime ever installed.
content: Delete unavailable devices and old runtimes to reclaim tens of gigabytes.

name: Store timestamps as UTC, format at the edge
abstract: All persisted timestamps are UTC; local time is applied only at display time.
overview: Storing local time makes ordering ambiguous across DST transitions.
content: Persist RFC3339 UTC. Convert to the viewer's zone in the presentation layer only.

name: Billing service shares the analytics pool
abstract: The billing reporting job reads from the analytics replica, not the primary connection pool.
overview: Keeps long analytical scans off the transactional pool.
content: Billing reports run against the read replica with a separate pool of 5 connections.

name: Auth audit log retention extended to 400 days
abstract: Authentication audit events are retained for 400 days to satisfy an annual review.
overview: Previous 90-day retention did not cover a yearly audit cycle.
content: Audit rows move to cold storage after 30 days and are purged at 400.

name: Canary at 5% for 10 minutes
abstract: New Atlas releases go to 5% of traffic for 10 minutes before full rollout.
overview: Ten minutes covers a full cache-warm cycle.
content: Canary aborts automatically if error rate exceeds baseline by two standard deviations.

name: Config is TOML, not YAML
abstract: Beacon configuration uses TOML because YAML's implicit typing caused version-string bugs.
overview: YAML parsed 1.10 as a float and silently truncated it.
content: TOML requires explicit quoting, which removes that class of bug.

name: Only retry idempotent operations
abstract: Retries are permitted only for operations carrying an idempotency key.
overview: Retrying a non-idempotent write duplicates side effects.
content: Every retryable request carries a client-generated idempotency key the server deduplicates on.

name: Warn is for actionable conditions only
abstract: Beacon reserves warn for conditions a human should act on; everything else is info or debug.
overview: Warn-level noise trains operators to ignore warnings.
content: If nobody would change their behaviour because of a line, it is not a warning.
